description: The judgements of the solver as data. A kind is one function of editor/solver.js; a record is one judgement with its id, and a line of a kit it made carries that id, so a wrong line points at its judgement or at the engine.

judgements.says: {0} on the pins of its IO MUX
judgements.why: A host on the pins of its own IO MUX runs at its full speed, and wired boards often take them: SPI3 of the terminal and of dotview-clock is on 23 and 18. Taken only when every line of the host is free there; a pin the solver keeps out, as a strapping pin, leaves the host to other pins, so SPI2 of an ESP32, whose MISO is GPIO 12, is not on its IO MUX in a kit while the terminal has it there.

judgements.says: {0} is a strapping pin ({1}): nothing on it should hold a level of its own at reset
judgements.why: A strapping pin is sampled at reset. The datasheet gives what it selects and the rows of the table of boot modes (gpio.boot_modes, gpio.pins.*.boot of the chip); the solver reads from them the harm of a level there: run, where the start of the program or the voltage of the flash depends on it, download, where only a download mode does, none otherwise. The kit keeps out the harms listed here and a strapping pin the datasheet does not describe; it may take the others, as GPIO 5 of an ESP32, which the terminal takes for a CS.
